title: Who administers AI Guard: system users and RBAC roles

prose.text: AI Guard administrators are system users; what each may do is set by an RBAC role.

checks.do: The administrator's role in System User Management and that role's scope on the module in question, including whether it can view prompts.

system-users.statement: System users are managed through the Authentication Service admin portal and can be viewed in AI Guard: the System Users page under System User Management shows each user's name, email, login type, role, creation date and last-updated date, and system users can be added and edited (name, email and role) from it.

quotes: System users are managed through the Authentication Service Admin Portal, but you can view them within AI Guard.
Name: Name of the system user.
Email: Email address of the system user.
Login Type: Displays the method of user login.
Role: Role of the system user such as Administrator or Editor.
Created At: Date that the system user was created.
Last Updated At: Date that the system user's information was last updated.
Enter the Name, Email, and Role for the system user and click Submit.
Under the Action column, click Edit. The Edit System User window appears.
Edit the Name, Email, or Role for the system user and click Update.
In the AI Guard left-side navigation, go to System User Management. The System Users page appears.

rbac-scope.statement: AI Guard RBAC applies to system users managed through Authentication Service and to system users hosted locally in AI Guard.

quotes: System users provisioned/managed through Zscaler Authentication (Authentication Service).
Local hosted system users in AI Guard.

rbac-permissions.statement: A role combines per-module permissions with scopes: most modules (Policies, LLMs, Private AI Apps, Log Exports, User Management, RBAC Management) take None, View, Create, Edit or Delete; Dashboard, Insights, Topology and Audit Log take None or View; Policy Testing None, View or Create; Tenant Settings None, View or Edit; API Clients None, View or Delete.

quotes: | Default Access (applies permissions to all modules) | None \| View \| Create \| Edit \| Delete |
| Dashboard | None \| View |
| Topology | None \| View |
| Policies | None \| View \| Create \| Edit \| Delete |
| Policy Testing | None \| View \| Create |
| Audit Log | None \| View |
| Tenant Settings | None \| View \| Edit |
| API Clients | None \| View \| Delete |
| Insights | None \| View |
| LLMs | None \| View \| Create \| Edit \| Delete |
| Private AI Apps | None \| View \| Create \| Edit \| Delete |
| Log Exports | None \| View \| Create \| Edit \| Delete |
| User Management | None \| View \| Create \| Edit \| Delete |
| RBAC Management | None \| View \| Create \| Edit \| Delete |

templates.statement: Role templates are Viewer (read-only access to all modules), Editor (read, create and update, no delete) and Administrator (full access to all modules).

quotes: Viewer: Read-only access to all modules.
Editor: Read, create, and update access. No delete access.
Administrator: Full access to all modules.

view-prompts-separate.statement: The page's example roles give Dashboard and Insights View while leaving Events (View Prompts) unchecked, so seeing prompt content is a permission of its own.

quotes: Dashboard: View
Events (View Prompts): None (unchecked)
Insights: View

assign.statement: Roles are assigned to system users from System User Management, by editing or adding a system user and picking the role.

quotes: In the Edit System User or Add System User window, click the Role drop-down menu and select the role you want to assign.
